summary: Phase 2 acceptance at 15031cbe: P2-1 to P2-6 and P2-8 to P2-13 pass, PROJECT_TESTS pass (11 files, 155 tests), operating rules a to f pass. P2-7 fails: inspectPictureRow reports 22 of 29 delivered color PNGs with a non-white corner (class C rule, all four corners 250 or higher; the bottom-left corner measures 244 to 249). The maker claim 'files checked: 58, problems: 0' came from a narrower check. The delivery writer did not enforce the corner rule for these files.
blocking_findings: F1 [Blocker] phase-acceptance: P2-7 problems: 22. inspectPictureRow (class C white-corner rule, src/storytime/book-pictures.ts:1748, needs each of the four corner pixels at 250 or higher in all channels) fails 22 of 29 delivered color PNGs. The bottom-left corner pixel is 244 to 249 (examples: l2-w04-card-dad-v1.png 244,246,246; l2-w06-card-boat-v1.png 245,245,245; l2-w04-card-mom-v1.png 245,245,242). Only 7 color files pass (girl, goodbye, astronaut, cap, sandwich, pot, teddy). The maker log jr-green-29344ae.log and plan Task 7 report 'files checked: 58, problems: 0', but that count came from a check of size, 8-bit depth, and alpha only, so it is not the P2-7 check (A5). Rationale: test-strategy P2-7 requires inspectPictureRow and 'problems: 0'. All 29 line art files pass inspectLineArtPng (widths 12 to 28 px). A fix is a decision: re-run color and line for the 22 rows, or an owner record that the card color files may keep a near-white corner.
nonblocking_findings: F2 [Nit] phase-acceptance: plan Task 7 cites SHA 29344ae4 and MANIFEST.txt source-commit cites 29344ae4, but the commit message of 29344ae4 is 'family line try 3' and the delivery commit is ac2502f3 (the Task 7 evidence is in jr-green-29344ae.log). Task 6 cites a0969f77 but the row closed at 4c307cce. Rationale: a task SHA should name the commit that holds the task evidence; the Phase 1 convention (128b6c12) was not re-checked in this run.

F3 [Nit] phase-acceptance: P2-13 text scan found the provider name 'OpenRouter' in spec-review-7af682d and spec-review-ac5acf0 logs and JSON. Each hit is a name in prose, with no key or token. Rationale: reported so the scan result is traceable; the case-sensitive patterns sk-, OPENROUTER, and Bearer give no secret.
